description: Canonical registry of verifiable claims that a Chio kernel can make on behalf of a tenant. Every signed artifact and every behavioral guarantee a verifier can check has a row here.

claims.summary: A CapabilityToken carries a signature from the issuing authority over the canonical body.
A receipt carries the kernel's signed verdict for a single mediated tool call.
A delegated child capability scope is a subset of its parent (no privilege amplification).

Peers exchange a feature bitset and a maximum capability-token schema at handshake time. The verifier rejects inbound tokens whose schema exceeds the negotiated ceiling, blocking a v1-only Mallory from forcing a v2-aware Alice to parse v2-only fields.

A v2 CapabilityToken's budget_share_bps is enforced not just per-token (<= 10000 bps) but as a sibling-sum across delegated children of a common parent. The verifier consults a BudgetRegistry at the verify step and rejects any child whose admission would push the running sum past the parent's own share.

A v2 CapabilityToken carries an on-the-wire attenuation_proof witness; verifiers check the witness hashes and subset relation fail closed AND require attenuation_proof.parent_scope_hash to be bound to the trust-root scope hash (direct issue) or the last delegation link's signed scope_hash (delegated chain).

Every kernel/guard/adapter outbound HTTP path declares a typed HttpEgressContract and runs through chio_egress_contract::send_with_contract (or the URL-only enforce_url helper for non-reqwest substrates) before bytes leave the substrate. The contract validates target URL on the initial request, every redirect target, and the response body size; loopback, link-local, IPv6 ULA, unbounded redirects, and oversize responses fail closed. A workspace lint at scripts/check-http-egress-contract.sh catches regressions; new callers must thread the contract through their config.

A chio.anchor_batch.v1 signs a Merkle root over N receipts/checkpoints and can bind that root to a public witness lane through AnchorWitnessClient. Per-receipt local signatures stay authoritative. The enforced subset recomputes Merkle roots/proofs, checks witness root/body-hash binding, verifies Rekor signed-entry timestamps, rejects sync self-asserted Witnessed under require_public_witness, rejects OTS marker-only receipts as advisory until trusted Bitcoin header or calendar-backed commitment evidence exists, and admits Stale only from a verifier-owned batch_body_hash -> verified_at cache. Rekor Merkle inclusion-proof checking, OTS trusted-header verification, and formal public-witness anti-equivocation remain proposed evidence.

A v2 receipt is content-addressed by body_hash := H(canonical_jcs(ReceiptV2BodyHashInput)) where the input set strictly excludes body_hash, signature, and the legacy UUIDv7 receipt_id. The kernel mints `ChioReceiptV2` on the production hot path when the negotiated peer profile advertises `accepts_receipt_v2`; the legacy UUIDv7 alias is non-authoritative for replay (replay key is body_hash).

proposed_claims.summary: Multi-parent receipt lineage carries a signed dag_ordinal + HLC triple; verifier predicate child.dag_ordinal > max(parent.dag_ordinal) rejects cycles across independent kernel clock domains.
Capability tokens, federation handshake envelopes, and receipts accept a hybrid:<classical>:<pq>:<alg_set> signature wire format with the algorithm enum value 'hybrid'.
Federation handshakes bind a Bronze, Silver, or Gold conformance tier into the signed challenge, and quorum policy rejects peers below min_tier before admission.
